statement: Familia Fernández Rivera traces its family wine enterprise to Alejandro Fernández and Esperanza Rivera, whose first wines were made from family vineyards in 1972; the current enterprise presents four wineries and says their granddaughters took charge of the group in 2019.
Condado de Haza is a Familia Fernández Rivera winery/estate in Roa, Burgos, with 200 hectares of vineyards and a current commitment to 100% organic production.

Alenza Gran Reserva is produced by Condado de Haza in the Ribera del Duero wine world; the 2019 first-party page identifies it as 100% Tempranillo from the Maricalva vineyard and describes the name as a tribute to Alejandro Fernández and Esperanza Rivera.

The Maricalva source described for Alenza 2019 is presented as own vineyard land in the municipal areas of Roa and La Horra at roughly 800 metres, on clay soils with sand and gravel in varying proportions.
For the 2019 Alenza Gran Reserva, Condado de Haza documents 27 months of aging in American oak and identifies stem use from Maricalva fruit as part of the wine's identity.
Within Ribera del Duero, the principal grape Tempranillo is also known as Tinto Fino and Tinta del País; these are regional names for the same grape identity, not separate biological varieties.

Current Ribera del Duero specifications require red Gran Reserva wines to age for at least 60 months in total, including at least 24 months in oak barrels of no more than 330 litres, with the remainder in bottle.
Scar of the Sea was established in 2012 and is currently owned and operated by Mikey and Gina Giugni in San Luis Obispo, California.

Mikey and Gina Giugni acquired Bassi Vineyard in 2024; independent reporting identifies them as majority owners with Will and Coral Frischkorn as partners, while Scar of the Sea had been purchasing Bassi fruit since 2019.
Scar of the Sea places Bassi Vineyard in the hillsides of Avila Valley, about 1.2 miles from Avila Beach, facing south on sandstone soils; the site is within the San Luis Obispo Coast AVA.

Scar of the Sea states that Bassi Vineyard completed conversion and received Demeter biodynamic certification in July 2024; the producer currently describes all 42 acres it farms across four SLO Coast sites as Demeter-certified biodynamic farming.
Scar of the Sea produces a recurring Bassi Vineyard Chardonnay from the Bassi site within the SLO Coast AVA; current trade documentation describes it as 100% Chardonnay.

For the currently documented 2023 Bassi Vineyard Chardonnay, specialist importer technical material describes whole-cluster pressing, native-yeast fermentation in neutral French oak, natural malolactic fermentation, 19 months on lees, a 10% component from a Bassi Chardonnay solera begun in 2019, unfined/unfiltered bottling and minimal sulfur.

scope_notes: Directly evidenced cross-world contact, but material transfer should not be encoded as completed propagation until a later source confirms it occurred.
statement: The Bassi world has direct, not merely geographic, contact with the existing Phelan Farm world: Phelan Farm's own site lists a 2021 Brij Bassi Syrah among purchased-grape wines, and 2024 reporting says Raj Parr agreed to supply Pink Chardonnay cuttings from Phelan Farm for Bassi replanting.
resolution_needed: Confirm whether the announced Pink Chardonnay material transfer and planting occurred before creating a PROPAGATED_FROM edge; independently resolve Brij as a project before modeling its Bassi fruit-purchase edge.

statement: Ashes & Diamonds is a Napa winery launched in 2017 by proprietor and owner Kashy Khaledi.
Ashes & Diamonds identifies Steve Matthiasson as winemaker for its Cabernet Franc line, including Diamond Vintages 2016–2018, Cabernet Franc №6 in 2019 and Cabernet Franc №10 in 2023.

scope_notes: Release numbers are temporal presentation metadata within a continuing Cabernet Franc line and should not become separate durable wine entities solely because the number changes.
statement: Ashes & Diamonds presents Cabernet Franc as a continuing Napa Valley wine line whose release number changes over time, including №6 for 2019 and №10 for 2023; CARTA therefore models one durable Ashes & Diamonds Cabernet Franc identity rather than a separate wine entity for each number.

The exact cellar seed, Ashes & Diamonds No 3 Cabernet Franc 2016, is documented as a Napa Valley red composed of 80% Cabernet Franc and 20% Merlot at 13.5% alcohol; Ashes & Diamonds now groups 2016 and 2018 Cabernet Franc as Diamond Vintages from Ashes & Diamonds Vineyard.

Ashes & Diamonds Vineyard is at the estate in the Oak Knoll District of Napa Valley; its Cabernet Franc block was planted in 1986 to Clone 214 and the vineyard is farmed organically with minimal irrigation.

Ashes & Diamonds Cabernet Franc cellar details vary by release: №6 2019 was aged 19 months with 16% new French oak, while №10 2023 was aged 17 months with 35% new French oak; these are release-specific facts, not timeless properties of the wine.
TTB lists Napa Valley as an established California American Viticultural Area, first established January 28, 1981; Oak Knoll District of Napa Valley is a nested AVA within Napa Valley.
Guillaume Gilles is an independent vigneron based in Cornas; specialist sources document his own domaine from 2007 and the Cornas producer association lists him at 1 Grande Rue, Cornas.

Robert Michel mentored Guillaume Gilles; Vine Trail says Michel offered Gilles an apprenticeship in 2000 and that Gilles worked with him until Michel's 2006 retirement, while Rosenthal explicitly calls Gilles Michel's protégé.
After working with Robert Michel through 2006, Guillaume Gilles completed a stint with Jean-Louis Chave in Hermitage before starting independently in 2007.
Vine Trail identifies Cornas vigneron Marcel Juge as Guillaume Gilles's grandfather and describes Juge as an early personal reference point for Gilles's desire to work in wine.

Guillaume Gilles Les Peyrouses Rouge is a Syrah wine bottled as Côtes du Rhône, from an old-vines parcel on the flats in the commune of Cornas; Rosenthal describes the site's soils as sand and clay overlain with large galet stones.

INAO defines Cornas AOP as a red-wine appellation delimited on the sole commune of Cornas and produced only from Syrah; physical location in the commune does not by itself prove that a parcel falls within the delimited AOP.

Côtes du Rhône is a regional AOP extending along the Rhône valley between Vienne and Avignon; Guillaume Gilles's Les Peyrouses Rouge is presented by his specialist importer under this AOP rather than as Cornas.

Vine Trail reports that Guillaume Gilles became certified organic from 2020 and describes hand vineyard work, whole-bunch red fermentation, native yeasts, no fining or filtration, and restrained sulfur use.
